title: Ode to the First Day of the Year
text:
We distinguish it
as

if it were
a little horse
unlike all
other horses.

	We adorn
its forehead
with a ribbon,
we fasten
around its neck
	red bells,
and at midnight
we go to welcome it
as if it
	were
an explorer descending from a star.


As bread resembles
yesterday’s bread,
as one ring all other
	rings:
the days
blink,
bright, tinkling, fugitive,
and lie
	down in the dark night.


I see the last
day
of this
year
on a railway, heading toward the
	rains
of the distant purple archipelago,
and the man
of the
	engine,
intricate as a clock in heaven,
lowering his eyes
to
	the infinite
score of the rails,

to the gleaming cranks,
to the swift linkages of fire.

	O driver of trains
run wild
toward the black
stations of the
	night,
is this ending
of the year,
without wife or children,
not the same as
	yesterday’s, as tomorrow’s?
From the tracks
and the railway shops,
the first
	day, the first dawn
of a year beginning,
the first day, the
	first dawn
of a year beginning,

has the same rusted
color of an iron train:
and the beings
along the
	way salute it,

the cows, the villages,
in the steam of dawn,
not knowing
that this
	is

the gateway of the year,
a day
shaken
by bells,

	adorned with feathers and carnations.


The earth
does not
know it:
it will receive
this day,
golden, gray,
	sky-blue,
spread it over hills,
wet it with
arrows
of

	transparent
rain,
and afterward roll it up
inside its tube,
store it
	in shadow.


So it is, but,
little
gateway of hope,
new day of the year,

	though you are the same
as loaves of bread
are like all bread,

we are going to live you differently,
we are going to eat you, to flower, to
	wait.
We shall set you
like a cake
inside our life,
we shall
	light you
like a candelabrum,
we shall drink you
as

if you were a topaz.
Day
of the new
year,
electric day,
	fresh,
all
the leaves emerge green
from the

trunk of your time.
Crown us
with
water,
with open

	jasmines,
with every fragrance
unfurled,
yes,
though
you may only

	be
one day,
one poor
human day,
your halo
pulses
above
	so many

weary
hearts,
and you are,
O new
day,
O cloud
	to come,
bread never seen,
enduring
tower!
editorial_note: The ode’s humble analogy between a new day and daily bread is preserved alongside its ceremonial horse, railway, and topaz; vivirte remains the direct, active promise to live the day.
